name: comp-167

frames.best_why: Neutral is chosen with a light ring, all five faces are clear, and no cursor covers them.

tagline: Five emoji faces in circles ask you to rate how it went.
summary: A one-row sentiment picker: five round radio buttons, each wrapping an emoji from angry to laughing, under the question How did it go? The chosen face takes a brighter ring.
appearance: A white question sits left-aligned above five equal circles joined in one row on black. Each circle is a thin grey outline around a large emoji face, running from an angry frown to a wide grin.
behaviour: Clicking a face selects it and lightens its ring; keyboard focus adds a second outer ring. The clip begins on Neutral and finishes on Sad.
demo_content: How did it go? heading with five faces from angry to laughing
search_phrases: rate how you feel with emojis
how did it go feedback faces
use_when: Asking for a fast one-tap mood or satisfaction score right after a task or a chat.
avoid_when: No words name the faces on screen, so the scale rests on the emoji meaning the same to everyone.
customise: Faces come from an items array inside the file; change the emoji or the stored labels there. Circle size, gap and ring colour are utility classes in the same file.
weight_why: Five small circles with emoji glyphs and a short ring colour fade.

a11y.note: The labels defined in the data are never rendered, so each face is named only by its emoji character; arrow keys and a visible focus ring still work.

issues: The written labels in the data are never shown, so a face is announced only as its emoji.
polish_why: Tidy row and a friendly, quick idea; nothing on screen gives the faces words.
title: Emoji Sentiment Picker
